title: Rivalry with Dick Boom over booking
summary: A competing agent resented Thomas for tying up territory, refused to book with him, then joined his office.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I know there was a guy that used to live in your(?) neighborhood that you were connected with...
What happened with you and him, and what was that about? Where did that come out?
Well, he didn't like me... He didn't like me, because if he had an attraction to book in this territory, my territory, he couldn't get through. Because see, I booked...
No. He was working for Universal. I was working for Shaw.
So you never worked for him, then.

No. He worked in the office with me. I worked under him. He kind of finally came to the office where I was working. But he hated me, because if he had a big attraction and called some of the big places to put

them, there was no openings. Because I used to book them guys up two and three weeks at a time. And they'd know I always had somebody to book 'em with in two weeks, because they only needed two weeks to promote.

Yeah. So he took a hating to me. Because one guy, he called...the guy called him to get a date on an artist he had, and he told the guy... This is when I first found it out. He said he called him, and he said, "Call Walter Thomas; I ain't got nothin' for you." But he was that kind of guy. He was a Dutchman, and he hated me...

And when he came to the office, I had breakfast with him one morning. I said, "Man, it don't make sense that we got a hassle going on. Especially if we're going to work together." Because I was at the office before he got there; they'd just brought him in.
Well, it wasn't that you had lost these people. It was that your agency lost these people.
But there was no way for you to... (?) the owners(?) if you don't book them, there was no way for you to get to be like a personal... A lot of those (?) personal managers make a lot of money...
